newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ARSENAL CARETAKER MANAGER HOUSTON QUITS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARSENAL CARETAKER MANAGER HOUSTON QUITS.

text.p: Troubled Arsenal said on Friday that their caretaker manager Stewart Houston had quit.
The premier league club immediately put former Northern Ireland star Pat Rice in charge for Monday's home game with leaders Sheffield Wednesday.
Houston took temporary charge for the second time in his Highbury career when Bruce Rioch was controversially sacked last month just five days before the start of the season.
Houston has been linked recently with a move to Leeds, where ex-Arsenal manager George Graham took charge on Tuesday, and Queens Park Rangers, who parted company with Ray Wilkins last week.

Houston had nearly two years of a recently-signed contract to run and had originally been expected to remain under Frenchman Arsene Wenger, who is set to be confirmed as the new Arsenal manager, possibly next week.
Arsenal said in a statement: "Stewart Houston has today tendered his resignation as assistant manager, which, with great reluctance, the board have accepted."
Graham, preparing for his first match in charge of Leeds at Coventry on Saturday, refused to confirm reports that Houston was set to become his assistant.
"I have no comment to make at all on these reports," he said.
